Evaluation plan for mixed short-prompt / long-generation serving (corpus-01201).

Performance-analysis framing.
Primary falsifiable hypothesis H-P: enabling chunked prefill (chunk = 512 tokens)
on the production mix reduces short-prompt TTFT P99 by >=25% at fixed QPS while
degrading output-token throughput by <=5%. Null H0: no change in TTFT P99 beyond
trial noise (overlapping bootstrap CIs).
Controlled experiment: single-variable A/B on the same node, same weights hash,
same seeded workload trace replayed identically to both arms, randomized arm
order across >=5 trial pairs. Mechanism being tested: chunking bounds the length
of any single prefill occupancy of the scheduler step, so decode steps interleave
and head-of-line blocking of short prompts shrinks; the cost is more scheduler
iterations and reduced prefill arithmetic intensity.
Boundary conditions: the effect should be near zero when prompts are uniformly
short (no long prefill to chunk) and should grow with the long-prompt tail. If
TTFT improves in the short-prompt-only cell too, the mechanism claim is wrong and
something else changed - discard the hypothesis.

0. Scope and non-claims
This is a serving-system measurement protocol only. It characterizes the
deployment (engine build, weights hash, quantization, scheduler policy, GPU SKU,
tenancy, workload mix), not model domain capability. No number here transfers
across any of those axes; changing one invalidates the baseline and requires a
re-run. Results are provisional until the falsification experiment below is
executed on real hardware.

1. Assumptions to record before any run (a run without these is unreportable)
- Engine + commit SHA (e.g. vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM), CUDA + NCCL version,
  driver version.
- Weights: repo + revision hash, dtype, quantization (fp16 / fp8 / awq / gptq),
  KV-cache dtype.
- Parallelism: TP / PP / DP degrees, `nvidia-smi topo -m` output, NVLink vs PCIe,
  NIC model and whether GDR is active (`ibv_devinfo`, NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL).
- Scheduler knobs: max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens, chunked-prefill on/off
  and chunk size, preemption/swap policy, gpu_memory_utilization.
- Workload: prompt-length and output-length distributions (report percentiles,
  not means), arrival process (fixed QPS Poisson vs closed-loop), mix ratio of
  short-prompt vs long-generation requests, and the RNG seed used to draw it.
- Client: request timeout, streaming on/off, concurrency cap, clock source.

2. Metric definitions (ambiguity here is the most common source of bogus deltas)
- TTFT = t(first token received by client) - t(request submitted by client).
  Includes queue wait. Also record queue_wait separately from server traces so
  TTFT can be decomposed into queue_wait + prefill_compute + network.
- TPOT = (t(last token) - t(first token)) / (output_tokens - 1). Report the
  per-request distribution, never a global mean; a global mean silently reweights
  toward long generations.
- Throughput: report output tokens/s AND total (prefill+decode) tokens/s AND
  requests/s. Output-token throughput alone hides prefill cost; total-token
  throughput alone hides decode stalls.
- Queueing: scheduler queue depth sampled at >=10 Hz, plus per-request
  queue_wait, plus preemption/recompute counters.
- P99 latency: end-to-end per request, reported with a bootstrap CI. P99 from
  fewer than ~3000 completed requests per cell is not interpretable; state n.

3. Why prefill and decode must be separated
Prefill is compute-bound and scales ~O(prompt_tokens) (attention adds an
O(L^2) term at long context); decode is memory-bandwidth- and KV-capacity-bound
and scales ~O(batch x model bytes) per step. Mixed traffic therefore has two
different bottlenecks that move in opposite directions under batching: raising
batch size improves decode bandwidth utilization but lengthens prefill-induced
head-of-line blocking, inflating TTFT of short prompts. Any single aggregate
number over the mix is unattributable. Run at minimum three cells:
  A short-prompt-only, B long-generation-only, C the production mix.
A and B calibrate the two regimes; C exposes the interference term. The
interference term is the quantity of interest: I = P99(C) - max(P99(A),P99(B))
at matched load.

4. Experimental protocol
- Warmup: discard the first 60 s or 300 requests, whichever is larger; report
  the discard rule. Warmup covers CUDA graph capture, autotuner, allocator
  steady state, and cache warmup.
- Load: closed-loop concurrency sweep AND open-loop Poisson QPS sweep. Only the
  open-loop sweep produces a meaningful latency-vs-load curve; closed-loop
  self-throttles and will hide queue collapse.
- Repeats: >=5 independent trials per cell, fresh server process per trial,
  randomized cell order to defeat thermal and cache drift. Report median of
  per-trial P99 plus interquartile range, not a pooled P99.
- Duration: each trial long enough that the steady-state window (post-warmup)
  contains >=3000 completions.
- Capture per trial: request-level traces (arrival, schedule, first token, last
  token, output length), scheduler queue depth timeseries, KV-cache utilization,
  preemption count, GPU memory (allocated + reserved + free), SM/DRAM utilization,
  power and clock throttle reasons (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks_throttle_reasons.active`),
  and for TP>1 the NCCL collective time distribution.

5. Confounders that must be controlled or measured
- Thermal/power throttling and clock drift across long sweeps.
- Noisy neighbours / other tenants on the same node or NIC.
- Client-side bottleneck: verify the load generator is not the limiter by
  doubling client cores and confirming numbers are unchanged.
- Tokenizer differences changing the effective token count of the same text.
- Autoscaling, retries, and load-balancer stickiness in front of the service.
- KV-cache reuse / prefix caching across trials, which makes trial 2+ artificially
  fast. Either disable prefix caching or explicitly report cache hit rate.
- Output-length variance: sampling temperature changes generation length, which
  changes throughput. Pin seed and max_tokens, or report length distribution.

6. Evidence required before any conclusion is accepted
Frozen baseline trace file + config manifest, >=5 trials per cell, CIs that do
not overlap for the claimed effect, the predicted counter moving in the predicted
direction, and a replication on a second identical node. Absent any of these,
the result is provisional.

7. Rollback / promotion gates
Promote a config change only if, on the production mix at target QPS:
P99 end-to-end does not regress >5%, TTFT P95 does not regress >10%, output-token
throughput improves >=10%, no increase in preemptions or 5xx/timeouts, and GPU
memory headroom stays >=5% below OOM. Roll back immediately on any of: error
rate above baseline+0.1pp, P99 above the SLO for 5 consecutive minutes, OOM or
engine restart, or KV utilization pinned at 100% with rising preemptions.
Canary at <=5% traffic for >=30 minutes before any wider rollout.

  regression exonerates the collective path.

baseline trace, and record the negative results - a hypothesis that predicted a
counter movement that did not occur is discarded, not re-explained.
